title: Learned feature selection identifies exploratory lymphedema-dose associations
summary: In76 treated head-and-neck cancer patients, an ensemble feature-selection analysis linked selected lymphatic-region dose features with recorded lymphedema. Subsequent competing-risk models described associations with external and internal swelling. These retrospective results do not establish a deployable forecast or causal dose effect.
ai_technology: Support vector machine recursive feature elimination; random forest; XGBoost; LASSO

evidence.tested: Learned feature ranking reduced clinicopathologic and dosimetric inputs before same-cohort competing-risk association analyses.
evidence.unknown: Selection and cutoff derivation reused the small cohort. Follow-up duration appeared among classification predictors, precluding an admission-time prediction interpretation. External/internal describe edema location, not independent validation cohorts. Prior cohort reporting, incomplete nesting and unmeasured confounding limit novelty and inference.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers rank and eliminate features, enabling exploratory dose-region association analysis.

source_review.scope: Actual primary cohort/endpoint, feature-selection/model and competing-risk Methods/Results/limitations; exact front/current notice metadata.
